entries.name: MIT OCW Economics
entries.description: Over 100 courses covering all major fields of economics. Courses include prerequisites, recommended textbooks, lecture slides, and assignments. Undergraduate and graduate programs.

entries.description: Introductory topics, few prerequisites.

entries.name: Khan Academy: Economics
entries.description: Elementary topics.

entries.name: Academic Search
entries.description: Search across .edu and other educational domains. These materials are more reliable than the big Internet.

entries.name: Foundational Equations of Economics
entries.description: These equations show principles behind "thinking like an economist". Graduate textbooks put these equiations in context.

entries.name: IGM Economic Experts Panel
entries.description: Top economists reflect on policy-related issues. Some answers contain useful details.

entries.name: AEA Resources for Economists
entries.description: A list of useful links maintained by the American Economic Association.

entries.name: RePEc
entries.description: Web services for economic researchers: bibliography, blog aggregator, new working papers, software.

entries.name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis: Web Services
entries.description: A list of helpful services.

entries.name: IDEAS RePEc
entries.description: The largest database of economics publications (2,000,000 items). Searching through papers is easier with Google: site:ideas.repec.org <search term>. Index sources mentioned below.

entries.name: NBER
entries.description: Working papers by major researchers. Many of these papers get published in peer-reviewed journal.

entries.name: SSRN Economics
entries.description: Working papers, no journal publications.

entries.name: Google Scholar
entries.description: Searching academic literature in general. Features author pages and citation counters. If you look for economic writings only, IDEAS would be more powerful.

entries.name: FRED2
entries.description: 380,000 (macro) time series from 80 sources. Supports plugins for importing data into Excel, Stata, R, and others. Has a mobile app.

entries.name: World Bank Data
entries.description: International macro time series. Has data import plugins.

entries.name: IMF Data
entries.description: The standard reference for macro data.

entries.name: Quandl
entries.description: Aggregate financial and economic data from multiple sources. Some data vendors sell their data via this service. Good integration with statistical software.

entries.name: MEDevEcon
entries.description: Data related to development economics.

entries.name: Monetary Economics: Data Sources
entries.description: Overview of macro data sources.

entries.name: OFFSTATS
entries.description: Links to official data sources by country and subject.

entries.name: International Open Government Dataset Search
entries.description: Over 1,000,000 government datasets. When works, this service looks like this. Otherwise, you'll see a 403 error.

entries.name: Dataset Search Engine
entries.description: Google-based search over 200 data sources, including those mentioned here. You can use Google search operators here.

entries.name: StackExchange Open Data
entries.description: If you haven't found the data you were looking for, you can ask it here.

entries.name: Reddit /r/datasets
entries.description: One more place to request datasets.

entries.name: Beamer
entries.description: A LaTeX class for presentations.

entries.name: TikZ
entries.description: An extension for drawing graphs. A how-to and a manual.

entries.name: LaTeX
entries.description: Economists write in LaTeX because it handles mathematics and references better than Word or LibreOffice. If you write regularly, LaTeX is worth learning.

entries.name: LyX
entries.description: A free and simple editor for LaTeX.

entries.name: Zotero
entries.description: Bibliography management. Also install (a) Zotero browser plugin to import papers from RePEc to your library; (b) Zotero-LyX plugin to cite literature easily.

entries.name: Git
entries.description: A version control system. Useful if you want to revert changes done months ago or collaborate with other authors. DropBox also has version control, but Git is more explicit. A short intro. Or use GitHub Desktop if you like it simple.

entries.name: Mendeley
entries.description: Bibliography management. Support synchronization on multiple plateforms: Mac, Windows, Ipad, Phone...

entries.name: IPython
entries.description: A Python-based environment. Econometric analysis is done with free packages: statsmodels, SciPy, NumPy, pandas.

entries.name: RStudio
entries.description: An R-based environment. R is the standard language among statisticians, so the R repositories often contain specialized libraries not available in other languages.

entries.name: Stata
entries.description: An industry standard for statistical computations in economics. Free alternatives:

entries.name: Julia
entries.description: High-level dynamic programming language designed to address the needs of high-performance numerical analysis and computational science.

entries.name: Matlab
entries.description: An industry standard for modeling and numerical optimization in economics. Free alternatives:

entries.name: Mathematica
entries.description: Symbolic computations. Free alternative

entries.name: GitHub
entries.description: A repository for code and data. Publishing research here is not a common practice, but it's more convenient that alternatives (university home page, DropBox, etc.).
